cases.question: What recalls are there for a 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists 6 recalls for the 2017 Honda Civic. None are marked "park it" or "park outside."

- 18V663000: Electric power steering. A magnet can come loose, which may cause steering assist in the wrong direction during a full lock turn. Dealers replace the steering gearbox free of charge.
- 18V817000: Owner's manual/child restraint information. The owner's information kit may be missing or incomplete. Dealers replace the kit free of charge. Covers Civic Hatchback and Type R.
- 18V266000: Air bags. Replacement seatback pads lack slits for the side air bags. Dealers replace the front seatback pads free of charge. Covers Civic Hatchback and Type R.
- 17V706000: Driveshaft. The right halfshaft may break. Covers Civic Sedan and Coupe. Dealers inspect and replace the halfshaft free of charge.
- 23V858000: Fuel pump. The pump may fail and stall the engine. Dealers replace the fuel pump module free of charge.
- 26V332000: Front passenger seat weight sensor. It may short and cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally in a crash. Dealers replace the sensor free of charge.

Several of these cover only certain body styles (sedan, coupe or hatchback). To tell you which ones apply to your car, I need your body style, or your VIN so I can look it up. You can also check the official status for your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

cases.question: Does my 2019 Hyundai Tucson have any recalls?

answer.text:
PARK OUTSIDE: NHTSA says to park your 2019 Hyundai Tucson outside and away from buildings until repaired under recall 20V543000.

This recall covers the anti-lock brake control unit (HECU), which can corrode and short electrically, possibly causing an engine compartment fire. The repair is free: dealers replace the HECU fuse, and for 2019 to 2021 models they also update the stability control software. Hyundai's number for this recall is 195, and you can call 1-855-371-9460.

To confirm your specific car's status, check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me your 17-character VIN, I can decode it to confirm the exact model and trim.
